title_en: -기 -- turning a verb into a noun
summary_en: Stem + 기 turns a verb or adjective into a noun ('doing X'), used with particles and in fixed frames like -기 싫다 and -기 쉽다.
ja_parallel: 〜こと／〜の、連用形名詞（読み・書き）
ja_diff_note: -기 covers only part of こと/の: Korean uses -기 for the action in general and in set frames (하기 싫다, 먹기 쉽다), but -는 것 for a specific fact (온 걸 알았다), while Japanese uses こと/の for both. Skill names like 읽기, 쓰기 line up with 読み, 書き.
notes: Stem + 기, no tense: 읽기, 걷기, 요리하기. It takes particles like any noun: 걷기가 좋아요, 요리하기를 좋아해요.
Fixed frames: -기 싫다 (don't want to), -기 쉽다/어렵다 (easy/hard to), -기 좋다/편하다 (good/convenient for), -기 시작하다 (start to); plus -기 전에 and -기 때문에.
With 좋아하다 both work (요리하는 것을 / 요리하기를 좋아해요), but for knowing or seeing a fact use -는 것: 비가 온 걸 몰랐어요.
To-do lists and goals often end in -기: 매일 30분 걷기.

examples.en: Ugh, I don't want to get up. It's Sunday.
examples.ja: あー、起きたくない。今日日曜じゃん。

examples.en: This neighborhood is great for walks.
examples.ja: この辺は散歩するのにいいですよ。

drills.prompt_en: Reading Korean is easy, but listening is hard.
drills.explain_en: 쉽다 takes a -기 noun ('reading is easy'), matching 듣기는 in the second half.

drills.prompt_en: It's raining, so I don't want to go out.
drills.explain_en: 'Don't want to' is the fixed frame -기 싫다.

drills.prompt_en: Grandma's place is near the subway station, so it's easy to get to.
drills.explain_en: -기 편하다 = convenient to do; the frame needs the -기 noun.

drills.prompt_en: I didn't know Seoyun was angry.
drills.explain_en: Knowing a specific fact uses -(으)ㄴ/는 것 (걸), not -기.
